subject: Boardwalk Health: hosting transition scope & networking constraints
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@boardwalk.health>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-15T16:05:00Z
Subject: Boardwalk Health: hosting transition scope & networking constraints

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick written summary so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps.

High-level goals you reiterated
- Migrate inference for the triage assistant off the hosted environment to a private VPC deployment (air-gapped possibility).
- Maintain sub-200ms p95 response for our 512-token baseline; batch throughput target ~200 reqs/min initially.
- Ensure logs/audit trail stay within Boardwalk region and KMS-managed keys.

Primary pain points
- Regulatory requirement to keep PHI inside their Nova region (no cross-region backups).
- Procurement needs a defined SOW with explicit network boundary and on-prem installation timeline to move to Legal.
- Concerns about key management and proof of deletion during decommission.

Technical constraints and asks you flagged
- No outbound internet from the inference enclave except to the customer-managed S3 endpoint and the KMS endpoint (whitelisted IPs).
- 10.0.0.0/24 is the preferred subnet for the initial VPC peering; they may prefer static routing rather than VPN.
- On-prem option: isolated rack with 2 x A100s (or equivalent) and no physical access for third parties.

Concrete next steps agreed
1) I will send a scoped checklist (network + security + ops) by end of day.
2) We schedule a 60‑minute tech deep dive with your infra + security (suggest Wed or Thu next week).
3) Boardwalk will loop in procurement and share their SOW template; Mateo to provide a first draft based on the checklist.

Attachments I will share in follow-up: Redwood Private hosting checklist (network + KMS items) and a short set of networking questions to speed the deep dive.

If I missed anything major, shout — otherwise I’ll schedule the deep dive and share the attachments by EOD.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment stubs: redwood-private-checklist.pdf (18KB), boardwalk-networking-questions.xlsx (9KB)

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@boardwalk.health>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@boardwalk.health
Date: 2026-09-15T18:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Boardwalk Health: hosting transition scope & networking constraints

Thanks Mateo — this captures the call accurately. A few clarifications from my side:

- We do require customer KMS only (AWS KMS key in Nova region). We cannot accept vendor-managed keys.
- For the outbound rule: allow only specific egress to our S3 (s3-nova.boardwalk.health) and the KMS endpoint; no other external domains.
- Timeline: procurement is targeting an SOW to Legal by 9/30; our infra team can do a tech deep dive next Thu (9/23) afternoon.

I’ve CC’d procurement so they can confirm the SOW template and timeline.

Sarah Lin
Director, Platform Security | Boardwalk Health
sarah.lin@boardwalk.health

Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@boardwalk.health
Date: 2026-09-15T20:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Boardwalk Health: hosting transition scope & networking constraints

Sarah — perfect, thanks for the timeline. I attached the two docs we discussed: the hosting checklist and a short networking questionnaire that will help your infra team prepare for the deep dive.

What I included in the checklist (high-level):
- Networking: required CIDRs, NAT/eBPF constraints, DNS allowlist, recommended peering patterns and MTU guidance.
- Security: KMS key handling, HSM options, how we map audit logs to your retention policy.
- Ops & runbook: deployment steps, rollback plan, and suggested canary traffic profile.
- Procurement notes: proposed SOW outline + placeholders for pricing and SLAs.

Requested info from Boardwalk before the tech deep dive
- Confirm the static egress IP range for KMS and S3 endpoints (or tell us if you need us to use your NAT gateway).
- Existing firewall rules for the 10.0.0.0/24 range.
- If you prefer DocuSign for SOW sign-off we can prepare the draft for procurement.

I’ll book the deep dive for Thu 2026-09-23 15:00 PT and send a calendar invite to the participants — if your procurement team prefers a tighter SOW timeline let me know and we can compress.

Thanks again,
Mateo

Attachments: redwood-private-checklist.pdf, boardwalk-networking-questions.xlsx

Subject: Internal: Boardwalk Health — owners & pre-call tasks

Folks — quick internal note after reading the thread (adding internal owners).

Owners
- Tech deep dive lead: Monica Patel (SE) — I’ll run the session and bring the infra playbook.
- Network deep dive: Karthik Iyer — handle routing, MTU, and peering patterns.
- Procurement support / pricing point: Mateo Alvarez — you have the SOW draft.

Pre-call items (we should complete before 9/23)
- Karthik: draft a one-page recommended peering diagram and list of constrained ports (target: 9/21).
- Mateo: prep SOW skeleton and pricing placeholders (target: 9/20).
- Monica: finalize demo runbook and a 20-minute infra checklist to walk Boardwalk through during the deep dive (target: 9/22).

I’ll also prepare a short slide (2–3 slides) that shows our KMS cosine: how we integrate customer KMS, key rotation, and proof-of-deletion flow — will drop it into the Drive folder and link in the invite.

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
